summary: **Risk: CRITICAL.** A vendor admin, working under change ticket CHG-48213, went far beyond the approved scope: queried customer PII, created a hidden sysadmin login (tmp_support), disabled Windows Defender, exported the PaymentCards table, uploaded it to personal cloud storage and then cleared the Security event log. Recommend immediate account suspension, credential rotation and incident response.

frames.description: RDP session starts; vendor authenticates to jump host JUMP-HOST-01 and completes an MFA prompt.
Windows desktop loads and the vendor opens the Start menu.
Vendor opens ServiceNow change ticket CHG-48213 in Edge to confirm the approved maintenance window.
PowerShell window opened; vendor runs hostname and whoami.
SQL Server Management Studio launched and connected to PROD-SQL-02 with a sysadmin login.
Object Explorer expanded; vendor browses customer_db tables including dbo.Customers and dbo.PaymentCards.
Query window opened; SELECT TOP 1000 * FROM dbo.Customers executed (not in the change ticket scope).
Query results show SSN and email columns in clear text on screen.
Vendor opens Security > Logins and inspects the sa and svc_backup accounts.
Creates a new SQL login 'tmp_support' and assigns the sysadmin server role.
'Enforce password policy' is unchecked for the new tmp_support login.
PowerShell: net localgroup administrators tmp_support /add executed on the database host.
Windows Defender real-time monitoring disabled via Set-MpPreference -DisableRealtimeMonitoring.
bcp exports dbo.PaymentCards to C:\Users\Public\export.csv.
export.csv compressed into a password-protected export.zip using 7-Zip.
Vendor opens a personal OneDrive in the browser and uploads export.zip to external cloud storage.
Upload reaches 100%; an anyone-with-the-link share URL is generated.
Security event log cleared with wevtutil cl Security.
export.csv deleted and cipher /w run to wipe free space (anti-forensics).
SSMS reopened to check SQL Agent job history for backup jobs.
Vendor returns to ticket CHG-48213 and marks the work 'Completed - no issues'.
Session idle; desktop with no active windows.
Session idle; screen unchanged.
Vendor signs out of the Windows session.
RDP disconnect dialog; session closes.

summary: **Risk: LOW.** Routine monthly patching on WSUS-01 matched change ticket CHG-48190. Only approved Microsoft updates were approved and validated; evidence was filed to the sanctioned SharePoint library. No anomalies observed.

frames.description: Vendor connects to patch-mgmt server WSUS-01 with a named service account; MFA approved.
Desktop loads; Server Manager opens automatically.
Vendor opens change ticket CHG-48190 (monthly OS patching) in Edge.
Windows Server Update Services console opened; Updates > Critical Updates listed.
KB5034441 and KB5034439 selected for approval to the Production-Servers group.
Approval dialog confirms install deadline for Saturday 02:00, inside the change window.
Update status report shows 42 of 45 servers compliant.
PowerShell: Get-HotFix | Sort InstalledOn -Desc | Select -First 5 on WSUS-01.
PowerShell: Invoke-Command to restart the Windows Update service on three lagging servers.
Command completes without errors; services report Running.
WSUS report refreshed; 45 of 45 servers pending install.
Vendor opens the internal runbook wiki page for post-patch validation.
Reads checklist items; no external sites accessed.
Test-NetConnection to the monitoring server; ping succeeds.
Event Viewer > Windows Update Client log reviewed; no failures.
Ticket CHG-48190 updated with patch list and marked 'Implemented'.
Session idle; Server Manager dashboard visible.
Session idle.
Vendor attaches the WSUS compliance report PDF to the ticket.
Compliance report copied to the approved SharePoint change-evidence library.
Ticket status confirmed as updated.
Session idle.
Vendor signs out of the session.
RDP disconnect dialog.
Session ended.

summary: **Risk: MEDIUM.** A contractor mostly performed legitimate read-only BI analysis, but also downloaded a sales workbook and sent it via personal webmail, browsed a file-sharing site and installed packages from an unapproved index. Needs a manager follow-up on the external email.

frames.description: Contractor connects to the shared analytics VM using a named contractor account.
Windows desktop loads; Outlook and Teams start automatically.
Contractor opens the internal wiki and the BI dashboard documentation.
Power BI service opened; Sales Overview report loaded.
Azure Data Studio connected to analytics-sql with a read-only login.
Query: SELECT region, SUM(revenue) FROM sales_summary GROUP BY region.
Results rendered as a bar chart; no sensitive columns present.
Contractor opens a personal webmail tab alongside the corporate dashboard.
Webmail inbox visible; a draft with an attachment named sales_q3.xlsx is open.
sales_q3.xlsx downloaded from the BI portal to the Downloads folder.
File attached to the personal webmail draft (not a corporate mailbox).
Webmail draft sent with sales_q3.xlsx to an external address.
Contractor opens a file-sharing website and browses the upload page.
Closes the file-sharing site without uploading.
Returns to Azure Data Studio; runs a second read-only query on sales_summary.
Windows Terminal: pip install pandas openpyxl run from an unapproved package index.
Python script executed to aggregate query results locally.
Script output saved to C:\Users\contractor\Documents\agg.csv.
Contractor reads internal documentation on the data catalog.
Teams chat window opened; discussing report requirements with an employee.
Session idle; no activity.
Session idle.
Contractor reviews the BI dashboard one last time.
Contractor signs out.
RDP disconnect dialog.
